extracted_tips: Basic step rhythm is 'quick, quick, slow' — think of it like a drum beat where every time your foot hits the floor it's a beat.
Pick up your feet with knees up ('up, up, up'). Don't flat-foot or you can't move fast enough for the quick steps.
Every step is a weight change — you take a step and immediately commit your weight so you're ready for the next move.
Partner hand hold: leaders palms UP, followers palms OVER. Never use thumbs — use 2 fingers (middle + ring, like Spider-Man) to cuff around the follower's fingers. Just relax, don't grip.
Right turn footwork: forward, forward, turn to the right. The turn happens on the slow count. Always end on the right foot because footwork is always right, left, right.
Stay on the line when turning right — turn right but don't drift forward off the line. Go right, then come back to center.
After the right turn, immediately go into basic: 'ta-ta-po' (back, back, forward). Full pattern is right turn then basic, repeating.
Leader signals the follower's right turn by lifting/picking up the hand on the second bar. Leader does 3 basics throughout — your forward does not change because you're not turning.
Use only ONE hand for the right turn — left hand holding follower's right. Do not hold with 2 hands. Signal on count 1, the turn happens on counts 2-3.
Hand flip trick during the turn: with the 2-finger Spider-Man grip, flip your wrist back as the follower turns, then flip it back down after. Cuff around her fingers, then release and re-catch.
Spotting during turns: pick a target, keep your eyes on it, bring your head right back to that target after rotation.
Leader's own right turn: forward, forward, turn. Left hand comes down, turn around, fingers rotate behind back, switch hand. Follower just keeps doing her basic.
